newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soap opera killer may be free in two years.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soap opera killer may be free in two years.

text.p: A Brazilian soap opera star who has been in prison for four years for the murder of his screen lover may walk free after only two more years behind bars, newspapers reported on Sunday.

A court in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday convicted 27-year-old Guilherme de Padua of the 1992 stabbing murder of his co-star Daniela Perez, and sentenced him to 19 years in prison. De Padua has already been in prison for four years awaiting trial.
Under Brazil's justice system de Padua would be entitled to conditional parole after serving a third of his sentence, which will be in March 1999, the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said.
In addition, prisoners are allowed after a sixth of their term to enter a "semi-open" regime, in which they can go out and work during the day but must spend their nights in jail.
De Padua would already be entitled to do that because of the time it has taken for the case to come to trial.
"Unfortunately, Brazil doesn't have laws that punish murder," Gloria Perez, mother of the murdered actress, told the Correio Braziliense newspaper.
A former male stripper turned soap opera star, de Padua was accused of murdering Perez with his former wife, 23-year-old Paula Thomaz. She will stand trial separately at a date yet to be determined.
The killing of Perez, 22, has gripped millions of soap opera fans, even outshining at the time the ongoing impeachment of disgraced former President Fernando Collor.

The trial has been covered intensely by the media and many Brazilians have watched every twist and turn as avidly as they followed the plot of the soap opera "De Corpo e Alma" (Of Body and Soul) in which de Padua and Perez starred.
De Padua shot to fame as the brooding lover of sexy teenager Yasmin, played by Perez.

During testimony that sounded straight out of a soap opera scene, he accused Thomaz of killing Perez in a fit of jealousy. The actress was stabbed 15 times with a pair of scissors, five of the blows puncturing her heart.
De Padua said he had had an affair with his co-star because her mother was the scriptwriter for the soap opera and it was in his "interests" to keep on her good side.
But the jury decided five to two that de Padua was lying and the judge labeled him "violent, perverse and cowardly."
Gloria Perez said she was satisfied that de Padua had been punished for his "lies" about her daughter.
But she demanded changes to the legal system.

"They (de Padua and Thomaz) should go to prison forever, so that they don't kill anybody else, don't hurt anybody else" she said in the interview with Correio. "But Brazilian law doesn't allow for that."
The Perez murder trial has been Brazil's equivalent of the famous O.J. Simpson case.
The courthouse in Rio was packed with journalists and television crews and national radio has carried the proceedings live since they began in the middle of the week.
Outside, several dozen protesters, including human rights groups, have camped out and demanded an overhaul of Brazil's justice system, where prominent defendants often walk free.
